title: Screen router: menus, overlays, pause, restart and back navigation
problem: Scattered change_scene calls cause duplicate HUDs, stale pause state, input held across transitions, and broken Android back behavior.
approach: One autoload owns the current screen and an overlay stack. goto() removes the old screen immediately (not at frame end), clears overlays, unpauses and releases held actions; overlays run with PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS and pause the tree. back() closes the top overlay, opens pause in gameplay, otherwise returns home and reports false at home so the caller can quit. Focus loss in a gameplay screen opens the pause overlay once.
prerequisites: Project Settings: application/config/quit_on_go_back=false for Android back handling
integration: lopodev knowledge apply godot-screen-router --project projects/<slug> --godot-dir projects/<slug>/godot
In a boot scene: ScreenRouter.register(&"main_menu", "res://scenes/MainMenu.tscn") for each screen, then ScreenRouter.goto(&"main_menu")
Buttons call ScreenRouter.goto(&"game"), ScreenRouter.open_overlay(&"pause"), ScreenRouter.close_overlay(), ScreenRouter.restart()
Set gameplay_screens and pause_overlay on the autoload if your names differ
expected_behavior: Exactly one screen node exists; pause/resume, restart, game over, return to menu and Android back behave predictably; no input stays held after a transition.
limitations: No transition animation; add a fade in goto() if needed
Screens are instanced under the root, not via change_scene_to_*

failure_modes.symptom: Two HUDs visible for a frame / double signal handlers
failure_modes.cause: queue_free() alone keeps the old screen in the tree until frame end

failure_modes.symptom: Android back quits the app from gameplay
